chapters.title: Launch
chapters.text: Voyager 2 launched first, sixteen days before Voyager 1, on a slower path that could reach all four giant planets.

chapters.title: Jupiter
chapters.text: It passed Jupiter four months after Voyager 1, and Jupiter's gravity bent its path towards Saturn.

chapters.title: Saturn
chapters.text: At Saturn the planets were lined up for one more assist, a chance that comes about once every 175 years.

chapters.title: Uranus
chapters.text: The first and still the only spacecraft to visit Uranus. It found ten new moons and two new rings.

chapters.title: Neptune
chapters.text: The only visit to Neptune so far, passing about 4,950 km above its north pole and then close to its moon Triton.

chapters.title: Interstellar space
chapters.text: Voyager 2 crossed the heliopause, the edge of the Sun's bubble of solar wind, six years after Voyager 1.

chapters.title: Launch
chapters.text: Voyager 1 launched on a faster path than Voyager 2 and reached Jupiter first.

chapters.title: Jupiter
chapters.text: Its images showed active volcanoes on Io, the first seen anywhere beyond Earth.

chapters.title: Saturn and Titan
chapters.text: A close pass of Titan bent its path up out of the plane of the planets, ending its planetary tour.

chapters.title: The Pale Blue Dot
chapters.text: Looking back from about 6 billion km, it photographed Earth as a single pixel.

chapters.title: Interstellar space
chapters.text: The first spacecraft to cross the heliopause into interstellar space.

chapters.title: One light-day
chapters.text: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth: a signal takes 24 hours each way.

chapters.title: Launch
chapters.text: Pioneer 10 was the first spacecraft sent to the outer planets.

chapters.title: Asteroid belt
chapters.text: It became the first to cross the asteroid belt, which took about seven months and showed the belt was safe to pass.

chapters.title: Jupiter
chapters.text: The first flyby of Jupiter, at 130,354 km, measuring its intense radiation belts.

chapters.title: Last signal
chapters.text: The last, faint signal came from 12.23 billion km. Pioneer 10 continues towards the constellation Taurus.

chapters.title: Launch
chapters.text: Pioneer 11 followed Pioneer 10 a year later.

chapters.title: Jupiter
chapters.text: It passed much closer than Pioneer 10, about 42,500 km from the cloud tops, and Jupiter's gravity sent it across the solar system to Saturn.

chapters.title: Saturn
chapters.text: The first spacecraft at Saturn, scouting the route through the rings for the Voyagers.

chapters.title: Last data
chapters.text: Its power fell too low to run the instruments, and the last engineering data came in November 1995.

chapters.title: Launch
chapters.text: New Horizons left Earth faster than any spacecraft before it.

chapters.title: Jupiter
chapters.text: A gravity assist from Jupiter cut about three years off the trip to Pluto.

chapters.title: Pluto
chapters.text: The first visit to Pluto, passing 12,500 km from the surface and showing its nitrogen-ice plains and mountains of water ice.

chapters.title: Arrokoth
chapters.text: The most distant object yet visited, a small, two-lobed body in the Kuiper Belt.
